sources.title: Calendar Resource Management README at v0.12.2
sources.locator: Configuration table, hierarchy, resource and restriction commands, identifier caveat and cron note (README lines 193-228).
sources.access_status: Opened successfully at exact full-SHA URL
observed_operations: web.open exact pinned URL in batch 1; inspected configuration lines
bounded_observations: Resource types include building, story/floor, room, general resource and vehicle; restriction commands are group-scoped; omitted boolean fields default false; child records require parent IDs; resources reach Calendar via cron/background jobs.
The README lists capacity, vehicle range and seating-capacity options without defining numeric types or units in the consulted text.
sources.limitations: The source does not establish behavior, privacy, support, or security of a deployed instance.

sources.title: Using the Calendar app, Nextcloud User Manual
sources.source_kind: official versioned manual served via latest URL
sources.version: Nextcloud 36 User Manual at access; latest URL is mutable
sources.locator: Sharing permissions (lines 74-85); event/timezone fields (149-162); room/resource conflict behavior and admin-managed backend requirement (220-230); trash default (263-272).
observed_operations: web.open exact URL in batch 1; focused opens at relevant sharing, timezone, resource and trash passages
bounded_observations: Calendar sharing is read-only or write, with write allowing event creation/edit/delete; event editor exposes separate time zones; later overlapping resource bookings are shown as rejected; administrators must install/configure resource back ends; calendar trash defaults to 30 days but is configurable.
sources.limitations: The manual is edition 36 while S04's listing tops out at server 35 for app 0.12.2. It is not proof that the documented behavior applies to that app/server pair.

sources.title: DAV & database commands, Nextcloud Administration Manual
sources.source_kind: official versioned manual served via stable URL
sources.version: Nextcloud 35 Administration Manual at access; stable URL is mutable
sources.locator: calendar:export and calendar:import formats and flags (lines 227-275).
observed_operations: web.open exact URL in batch 1; inspected calendar CLI sections
bounded_observations: calendar:export defaults to iCalendar; xCal and jCal are alternatives. Import validation values are 0/no validation, 1/validate and skip invalid, 2/validate and fail; error mode 0 continues by default and 1 fails on the first error. The command exports a calendar, not an evidenced whole-case repository.
sources.limitations: Does not establish task, case, note, or attachment export coverage and does not prove behavior on a different server release.

sources.title: Enable private resource bookings (hide event details, show only busy status), issue #196
sources.version: Opened 2025-09-13; issue remained open and labeled feature request at critic access
sources.locator: Issue state and description (lines 128-174); reporter's scoped workaround comment (189-199).
sources.access_status: Opened successfully; focused open inspected issue and comment
observed_operations: web.open exact issue URL in batch 2; focused open at issue description/comment
bounded_observations: The reporter says linking a resource to a private event exposes time/event in the resource calendar; the feature request remains open.

A comment proposes setting a user-owned resource calendar's share setting to show only busy. It specifically requires a real calendar owned by a user account that acts as the resource, then shared from that account; it is not stated as a general Calendar Resource Management fix.
sources.limitations: User issue and comment are not a code audit, support contract, or test of the specific app/server pair.

sources.title: Unauthenticated administrator account takeover through the legacy migration endpoint, GHSA-3356-vjx2-5pg8
sources.locator: Affected/patched versions, attack conditions and patch details (lines 130-179); technical detail (198-205).
sources.access_status: Opened successfully; focused find inspected version and exploit details
observed_operations: web.open exact advisory URL in batch 2; focused find for version and attack details
bounded_observations: The advisory describes unauthenticated administrator takeover through legacy migration; exploitation requires access to the endpoint and server connectivity to an attacker-controlled MySQL database. It applies to versions before 7.0.0; the 7.0.0+ patch makes the endpoint inert/removes web migration. The advisory states fixes are not backported.
sources.limitations: Applies to stated versions and attack path only; does not establish the security of later versions.
